indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a lavish film, a would-be epic, by retitling it Intolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' tells you to rearrange EPIC, I and MEANT. Intolerance is also the name of a famous silent epic film, which is what makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to put up with delay or annoyance is a form of intolerance, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Start to nose — i.e. ferret out

definitions.text: Start to nose — i.e. ferret out

indicators.note: out here means disordered or displaced, so the gathered letters are rearranged
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of nose is used

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin poking around and ferret out the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes N from nose; 'out' scrambles N with IE and FERRET. Read whole, the clue describes meddling: beginning to nose and ferret into others' business.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to stick your nose in and pry into matters that are not yours, exactly what the whole clue describes.

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pan is a hollow or depression in the ground, as in a salt pan

explanation.surface: A question about what policy the government took during the economic Depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests the 1930s slump, but here it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or intended course of action is a policy.

parts.note: draught is read as draught beer rather than a cold breeze: someone who resists every alcoholic drink, not merely beer on tap

explanation.surface: Advertising copy for window insulation that keeps out cold air better than most.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol refuses far more than draught beer.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tired parent observes that dull days make some children a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless weariness, the same as boredom.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying drink prior to wild revelry

indicators.note: prior to means before, so the drink comes ahead of the revelry

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, a drink
a riot is a scene of wild revelry, as in a riot of fun

explanation.surface: A car or float carries refreshments to a party before it gets out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA (tea, often spelt 'char' in Britain) precedes RIOT; 'carrying' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn two-wheeled vehicle used in ancient warfare and racing.

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are mixed up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook plans to serve a treat again, folding it into a larger feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeat' looks like a verb but is a noun: a taste that comes back after eating, as when food 'repeats' on you.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavour lingering or returning after you have eaten is the food repeating on you.

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: trips are slips or blunders
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A candidate makes mistakes and scores nothing in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the name of the final honours examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge University's degree exams are called the Tripos, so it is a particular examination.

clue.text: A sack stuffed with well-turned pastries

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with something has it packed inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: turned here means turned round, so the pastries word is read from its end back

parts.note: tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: Someone describes a bag packed with beautifully shaped pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like an article but is the definition, as in an A grade or A1 quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An A grade marks the top class, the highest quality.

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: to clear a sum is to make it as net profit

explanation.surface: A forester clears the ground around a spruce tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' looks like the tree but is the adjective meaning smart and tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means smartly kept and tidy, a synonym of trim.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pert means forward or cheeky

explanation.surface: A player was once skilful as a striker up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a football position but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Being highly skilled and knowledgeable is the same as being skilful.

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a minion is a servile follower or lackey

explanation.surface: A political party's flunkey has been placed in power.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion is sovereign control or rule, which is authority.

indicators.note: something sorted out is rearranged into order, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddle that the engineer Brunel tidied up is beyond counting.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a famous Victorian British engineer of railways, ships and bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too many to count is incalculable.

clue.text: Canopy formed by spreading trees after time

indicators.note: after places the trees piece behind the time piece
spreading means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Over time, spreading trees create a canopy of leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges TREES to ESTER, put after T. A tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester is the overhead hanging over a four-poster bed or pulpit.

clue.text: A hand with a fair variety of lines?

definitions.text: A hand with a fair variety of lines?

parts.words: A hand with a fair variety of lines?
parts.note: hand is read as a hired worker and lines as lines of work: a servant who turns to many sorts of job, not a palm with creases

explanation.surface: A palm reader examines a hand showing many different creases.
explanation.definitionFit: A general servant or jack of all trades handles many kinds of work.

clue.text: Virago caught up in troublesome matter?

definitions.text: Virago caught up in troublesome matter?

indicators.note: caught means held, so the reversed piece is held inside the scrambled one
troublesome suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged
in a down entry, up means the piece reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a nag is a scolding woman, a virago

explanation.surface: A shrewish woman is embroiled in some awkward business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NAG to GAN, which 'caught' puts inside TERMAT, a rearrangement of MATTER ('troublesome'). Read whole, the clue describes a shrew in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing woman, the same as a virago or scold.

clue.text: Cue ball's dead short? Who cares?

indicators.note: dead means completely and short means cut, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: red is one of the balls in snooker
a minder is someone who looks after or cares for another

explanation.surface: A snooker player shrugs off a cue ball that stopped short of the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cue' looks like the snooker cue but is the definition, a prompt. 'dead short' trims RED to RE; snooker uses red balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt that jogs the memory, which is what a reminder does.

clue.text: Hid diamonds on SE Greek island

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding pieces

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Someone buried jewels in the south-east of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: SE (south-east) is taken as printed; D follows SECRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something away is to put it in a secret place.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the following piece

parts.note: a charge is the price asked

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at what an accountant charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy!' looks like an exclamation of surprise but is a noun: a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim or fancy.

clue.text: Tenor — one rising audibly — is in voice

indicators.note: audibly means heard, so the pieces are judged by how they sound

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for tenor in music; a rebel is one who rises up in revolt

explanation.surface: A tenor whose voice is going up is singing.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, T plus REBEL sounds like the word wanted; 'one rising' looks like a pitch climbing but means an insurgent.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest boys' singing part is a treble, a type of voice.

parts.note: a bass is a fish
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film, an alien

explanation.surface: A dog finds a fish that looks foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound breed.

clue.text: Force shown by Henry in breaking impasse

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
breaking means smashing apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry uses force to break a deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges IMPASSE; 'in' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the force or stress given to something.

indicators.note: after places the right piece behind the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone feels perky after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means being quick, wide awake and lively.

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole combination reads backwards

parts.note: the French for 'the' is le, and the 's adds S
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is wild about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns round the whole run LES + MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman, a maid.

indicators.note: to just fail is to fall barely short, so the word stops one letter before its end

parts.note: to annex is to seize or grab territory

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly misses catching a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just fail to' trims ANNEX by its final letter. Queen Anne reigned over Britain from 1702 to 1714.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was a British queen, so the clue word names her by title.

definitions.meaning: a rasp for smoothing metal or wood
a folder or case for keeping papers

explanation.definitionFit: A file is a smoothing tool and also a container for documents, as in a box file.

clue.text: Overalls with brownish-grey grease all over the place

parts.note: dun is a dull brownish-grey colour

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Work clothes in a dull colour are smeared with grease everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing trousers with a bib, a kind of overalls.

clue.text: Improvement for gambler, paid for securing first in National

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the first letter is held inside the other piece

parts.note: to meet a cost is to pay for it, so met means paid for

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A punter's fortunes improve after the stake on the Grand National is paid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase horse race, which gives the surface its gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment means making something better, an improvement.
